Trastevere — Rome, Italy

Relatively safer day Average night

In detail

Trastevere is Rome's best-known nightlife and dining district on the west bank of the Tiber, a maze of narrow medieval streets that is quiet and picturesque by day but fills with bars, restaurants and crowds after dark. Local press regularly documents mala movida problems: in August 2026 a brawl involving around 15 mostly North African youths broke out in Vicolo del Bologna at 3am, with stones, glass bottles and pepper spray used and three men arrested; police have also carried out repeated crackdowns in 2026, including closing a venue for a week and arresting drug dealers working the alleys near the nightlife strip. Daytime Trastevere - residential streets, the market, Santa Maria basilica - shows no comparable issues.

Frequently asked questions

Is Trastevere safe?

Wandroz currently rates Trastevere in Rome, Italy as relatively safer than most other areas covered on Wandroz during the day and roughly average compared to other areas covered on Wandroz at night. This is a qualitative first-pass assessment based on general local knowledge and public reputation, not an official geolocated crime dataset — see the note on data limitations below before treating it as more precise than it is.

Is Trastevere safe at night?

At night, Trastevere is rated as roughly average compared to other areas covered on Wandroz. If you're unsure, it's worth checking recent local reviews for your specific street or block, since a neighbourhood-wide rating can't capture block-by-block variation.

Is Trastevere a good area to stay in as a tourist?

Trastevere's day rating (relatively safer than most other areas covered on Wandroz) is the more relevant one for typical daytime tourist activity; check the night rating too if you'll be out late.
